messages:
Alex: Quick RFC follow-up — allocator changes for Dedicated GPU pools. TL;DR: add tenant-level cost caps, prewarm budget, and a safety-headroom floor so the autoscaler never trims below X GPUs. Wanted to capture tradeoffs and an interface shape before I update the RFC.

Priya: +1 on safety headroom. One question: should cost caps be enforced as hard rejects or soft throttles? hard rejects will surprise customers.

Jon: soft throttle + backpressure signals to the runtime sounds better. We can emit an explicit 429-with-metrics that shows "cost-cap-hit" so client SDKs can surface guidance.

Megan: Prewarming is great for latency spikes, but it burns cost if unused. Can we make prewarm budget fractional or time-decayed? e.g. only keep prewarms for recent-peak tenants.

Rafael: Agreed re decay. Also need a clear eviction/preempt policy: reclaim prewarm for higher-priority tenants when capacity constrained. Otherwise we end up with noisy neighbors.

Alex: Sketch of config I had in mind:
```
autoscaling:
  min_pool_gpus: 2           # never below cluster-wide floor
  safety_headroom_pct: 12   # keep ~12% spare to absorb bursts
  prewarm_budget: 1         # GPUs to keep warm per high-usage tenant
  per_tenant_cost_cap_usd: 5000\/month  # soft cap, triggers throttling and alerts
  cost_cap_mode: soft       # enum: soft | hard
```
Would prefer keeping semantics simple for the API; fine-grained rules can live in operator config.

Priya: For cost caps, how about soft mode = throttle+notify, hard = deny new sessions and fallback to hosted? Must document fallback chain.

Jon: API shape needs to return a machine-readable reason: {code: "COST_CAP", mode: "soft", retry_after: 60}. That will make SDKs consistent.

Megan: On fairness: we should support both strict per-tenant caps and weighted shares. For multi-tenant Dedicated instances (internal teams), weighted shares > hard caps. For external customers, per-tenant hard caps make sense.

Rafael: Implementation note: allocator should use a two-pass decision. Pass 1: global feasibility (headroom + min_pool). Pass 2: tenant allocation respecting caps and weights. If pass2 fails, try eviction of prewarm or lower-priority workloads before returning deny.

Jon: Metrics we need surfaced in Console: per-tenant queue depth, cost burn rate (USD\/hr), prewarm-utilization, headroom_pct. Those feed Optimize suggestions.

Alex: Good list. Open question: default values. safety_headroom_pct=12 feels okay for 8+ GPU pools. For small pools maybe 20%. Should it be absolute GPUs or percent?

Priya: percent is easier for scaling across sizes. But also allow min_headroom_gpus so small pools get sane behavior.

Megan: Edge case: auto-scaler oscillation when many tenants hit cap simultaneously. We should add dampening and a cooldown per-tenant allocation change.

Rafael: +1. Also add a circuit-breaker for autoscaler when infra instability detected (e.g., node failures). Fallback to conservative min_pool.

Alex: Updated plan: I will change RFC to propose: (1) config schema with percent+min headroom, (2) cost caps default to soft, (3) two-pass allocator + eviction priority, (4) prewarm decay policy and preemptable flag, (5) cooldown windows and autoscaler circuit-breaker.

Jon: Can you add a small sequence diagram showing allocator decision flow? Helps infra folks.

Alex: Will add. Also: should we gate hard caps behind an enterprise toggle?

Priya: Yes, enterprise toggle for hard-deny is safer. We'll need SLO guidance for fallback.

infra-bot: policy-service:config update queued by Alex — plan: autoscaling schema v2, scheduled for canary deploy tomorrow 03:00 UTC. :construction:

Megan: Thanks — please include a migration path for existing Dedicated customers (mapping old caps to new defaults).

Alex: Will do. I'll update RFC and ping this thread when it's changed. Thanks for the feedback :thumbsup:
